Substantially upgrade the Nxeon native webmail's MAILBOX SETTINGS in /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15, Prisma, self-hosted Mailcow). Right now it's minimal (`components/customer/mail/MailSettings.tsx`: identity + a PLAIN-TEXT signature textarea, connection, aliases, store-only auto-reply, password). The owner says it's "a joke" and specifically wants a much richer SIGNATURE experience. Make it feel like Titan/Zoho/Gmail settings, fully themed to Nxeon (reuse `card`/`btn-*`/`input`/`label`/`section-label`/`glass` and the existing modal's section-rail pattern).

## Study first (do NOT run git or `npm run build`)
- `components/customer/mail/MailSettings.tsx` (the modal + its 5 sections), `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts` (`getMailboxSettings`/`saveMailboxSettings`/`saveAutoReply`/aliases/`resetPassword`), `components/customer/mail/MailClient.tsx` + `Composer.tsx` (how the signature is currently loaded and appended to outgoing mail — plain text below `-- `), `lib/mail/render.ts` (`safeHtml` sanitizer — REUSE it), `lib/mailcow.ts` (Mailcow API helpers + `mcGetMailbox`/quota if present), and the `Mailbox` model in `prisma/schema.prisma`.

## YOU OWN prisma/schema.prisma this wave
Add fields to `Mailbox` (additive, nullable/defaulted): `signatureHtml String?`, `signatureEnabled Boolean @default(true)`, `signatureOnReply Boolean @default(true)`, `signaturePlacement String @default("below")` (above/below quoted text), `replyTo String?`, `organization String?`, `autoReplyStart DateTime?`, `autoReplyEnd DateTime?`, `forwardingAddress String?`, `forwardKeepCopy Boolean @default(true)`. Keep the existing `signature` (treat as the plain-text fallback). After editing, run `npx prisma generate` (LOCAL only — do NOT run `prisma db push`; the parent applies it to the DBs).

## Build these sections
1. **SIGNATURE (the headline) — a real rich editor.** A `contenteditable` HTML editor with a formatting toolbar: bold, italic, underline, text color, font family + size, insert link, insert image (by URL, and if there's an existing upload endpoint reuse it — otherwise URL/data-URI is fine), bullet/numbered list, clear formatting, and an "insert horizontal rule". Live preview of exactly what recipients see. Toggles: enable signature, include on replies/forwards (`signatureOnReply`), placement above/below the quoted message (`signaturePlacement`). Store as sanitized HTML in `signatureHtml` (sanitize with `safeHtml` on SAVE and before preview — no script/style/on* /iframe; allow img/a/span/font styling). Derive a plain-text version for the text part. Provide a couple of starter templates (name+title+company block) the user can insert. Keep it robust (no execCommand crashes if unsupported — degrade gracefully).
2. **IDENTITY** — display name (from address), `replyTo` (validated email), `organization`. Show the sending address (read-only).
3. **AUTO-REPLY / VACATION** — subject + body + a DATE RANGE (`autoReplyStart`/`autoReplyEnd`, "only send between these dates"). Keep it store-only if Mailcow still has no reliable vacation endpoint (check `lib/mailcow.ts`) — but keep the HONEST amber notice already used; do NOT claim it sends if it doesn't. If Mailcow DOES expose a working vacation/auto-responder endpoint, wire it for real.
4. **FORWARDING** — forward a copy to `forwardingAddress` (validated), with `forwardKeepCopy`. Implement via Mailcow if there's a real mechanism (e.g. an alias `goto` to both the mailbox and the forward target, or a sync/forward endpoint — inspect `lib/mailcow.ts`); if no safe real mechanism exists, store it + show an honest "coming soon / stored" note like auto-reply. Never pretend.
5. **STORAGE** — show quota used / total (from `quotaMB` + a Mailcow usage lookup if available; else show the quota with a note). A simple meter bar (reuse existing meter styles).
6. Keep **Connection**, **Aliases**, **Password** sections (largely as-is; light polish only).

## Wire the signature into sending
Update `MailClient`/`Composer`: load `signatureHtml`+toggles per active mailbox; for a NEW message append the sanitized signature HTML to the HTML part (and plain-text to the text part); for reply/forward, only include it when `signatureOnReply`, and place it per `signaturePlacement` relative to the quoted block. Preserve the existing behavior when only the legacy plain-text `signature` is set (fallback).

## Actions
Extend `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts` (all `requireUser` + `resolveMailbox` ownership + rate-limited on writes): `saveMailboxSettings` grows to persist identity + signature fields (sanitize signature server-side too); add `saveForwarding`, extend `saveAutoReply` with the date range. Remember a `"use server"` file may only export async functions — put shared consts/types in a plain module.

## Constraints
- No new npm deps (no rich-text library — hand-roll the contenteditable toolbar). Sanitize ALL signature HTML with the existing `safeHtml` before storing/previewing/sending (prevent self-XSS / broken markup). Do NOT touch migration, resize, terminal, or cPanel files. Do NOT run git, `npm run build`, or `prisma db push`.
- Write/Edit may time out on a hook — fall back to Bash heredocs and verify.
- Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx prisma generate >/dev/null 2>&1; npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` (clean for your files).

Report: new schema fields, the signature editor's capabilities + how HTML is sanitized end-to-end, each section's real-vs-stored status (be honest about auto-reply/forwarding), how the signature flows into outgoing mail, and any Mailcow endpoints used.

I'm mapping out the implementation strategy now. The `MailboxInfo` object already provides `usedBytes` and `quotaBytes` which I can use directly for the STORAGE section, and `getMailboxes()` returns these values. However, `MailSettings` only receives a `mailboxAddress`, so I'll need to add storage information to what `getMailboxSettings` returns—either by computing the quota from `quotaMB` or fetching usage data through IMAP, though that approach might be inefficient.

The cleanest solution is to pass the current `MailboxInfo` (which already has `usedBytes` and `quotaBytes`) from `MailClient` directly into `MailSettings` as props, avoiding an extra server round-trip. Since `MailClient` already has access to the active mailbox object with these values, I'll pass `storageUsedBytes` and `storageQuotaBytes` into `MailSettings` and use those for the quota display.

Now I'm shifting focus to the Mailcow integration for handling forwarding and auto-reply features. Implementing the forwarding logic... I'm realizing Mailcow has a hard constraint: you can't create an alias with the same address as an existing mailbox. Since I can't verify a real forwarding mechanism exists in Mailcow itself, the honest approach is to store the forwarding settings in the database and display a note to the user that it's being handled by our system, similar to how auto-reply works. I'm settling on store-only forwarding to stay honest about what I can reliably implement without risking the user's actual mail setup. Now I'm moving on to designing the rich signature editor.

I need to substantially rewrite MailSettings.tsx with new sections for identity, signature, autoreply, forwarding, storage, connection, aliases, and password. The tricky part is organizing shared types and constants — I can export types from the "use server" file since TypeScript types get erased at runtime, and the existing setup already does this. But I should still figure out what consts need to be shared between client and server. The plain-text conversion from HTML signature is needed in both places — for generating the text part when saving and for previewing on the client — so I'll create a plain module at `lib/mail/signature.ts` that exports the conversion helper, signature templates, and constants like the max signature length, keeping it importable from both sides.

I'm checking whether `render.ts` can be safely imported on the client. It's a pure module with no server-only imports or directives, just string operations, so it's safe to use there for live preview and sanitization before sending. The server will also sanitize on save for defense in depth.

Now I'm adding the signature fields to the Mailbox schema...

Extending the MailboxSettings type... MailSettings will receive those props from MailClient's active mailbox. The `saveMailboxSettings` function needs to handle persisting displayName, signature fields (both plain-text and HTML versions), signature preferences, replyTo with email validation, and organization. I'll sanitize the HTML signature server-side and keep the plain-text version in sync as a fallback.

I'm restructuring so the signature editor sends its fields separately from the identity section—signature owns the HTML and preferences, while identity handles displayName, replyTo, and organization. Both feed into `saveMailboxSettings`, which accepts partial updates and only modifies the fields that are actually provided.

Writing the saveMailboxSettings function... Parsing date strings to Date objects or null, then validating that the start date doesn't exceed the end date before storing. Now I need to integrate this into the mail client and composer — loading the full signature settings into state, then extending the compose draft to include the HTML signature so the composer can build the final HTML body with proper placement.

For new messages, I can't inline HTML into a plaintext textarea like I do with plain text, so instead I'll append the signature at send time for both new messages and replies, letting the placement setting control whether it goes above or below quoted content.

Since the requirement is to preserve fallback behavior when only plain-text signature exists, I'm setting up a unified mechanism in Composer that checks for sanitized HTML signature first, then falls back to plain text.

Actually, it makes more sense to push the logic into MailClient — it can determine whether to include a signature based on the message type and user settings, then only pass the relevant signature fields to the draft. That keeps Composer simpler and centralizes the decision-making. I'll have MailClient maintain a signature object with enabled, html, plain, onReply, and placement properties, then use a helper function to extract just the fields that should go into the draft based on whether it's a reply.

For the actual composition, the text part is straightforward — just append the plain signature after the body since quoted text doesn't appear in the text version anyway. The HTML part is more complex, needing to assemble the user's content, the quoted block if present, and the signature in the right order depending on placement preferences.

Adding signature delimiters... I'll import the sanitization utility and use it defensively in the editor. Now I'm building the SignatureSection component with a contentEditable div and a toolbar that supports formatting commands like bold, italic, lists, colors, fonts, links, images, and horizontal rules — all wrapped in try-catch since execCommand is deprecated but still widely supported. I'll add a live preview box below that renders the sanitized HTML so users see exactly what their signature will look like. state variable to track the HTML for preview and dirty state. I'll use `onMouseDown` with `preventDefault` on toolbar buttons to preserve the selection before executing commands. For the color picker, I'll focus the editor and execute the foreColor command, accepting that the selection might be lost temporarily—it's a reasonable tradeoff.

I'm also considering a saved-range approach: capture the selection on blur so I can restore it if native controls like the color input or font selects steal focus.

For toolbar buttons, I'll use onMouseDown with preventDefault to keep the selection intact without needing to restore. But for controls that open pickers or prompts, I'll restore the saved range before executing the command.

I need to be careful with the editor's styling too — it needs to look good in the dark theme, but the signature itself is meant for light email backgrounds, so I'll render the editor on a lighter surface to show colors accurately. ## What was built

### New schema fields on `Mailbox` (all additive, nullable/defaulted)
`signatureHtml String?`, `signatureEnabled Boolean @default(true)`, `signatureOnReply Boolean @default(true)`, `signaturePlacement String @default("below")`, `replyTo String?`, `organization String?`, `autoReplyStart DateTime?`, `autoReplyEnd DateTime?`, `forwardingAddress String?`, `forwardKeepCopy Boolean @default(true)`. Legacy `signature` is kept and now used as the derived/plain-text fallback.

### Signature editor (the headline) — `components/customer/mail/MailSettings.tsx`
A hand-rolled `contentEditable` rich editor (no new deps) on a white surface for WYSIWYG fidelity, with a themed dark toolbar: **bold, italic, underline, font family, text size, text color, bulleted/numbered lists, insert link, insert image by URL, horizontal rule, clear formatting**, plus 3 insertable starter templates (Classic / Accent bar / Minimal, seeded from the identity). Every `execCommand` is wrapped in try/catch and `insertHTML` falls back to append, so it degrades gracefully. A selection is saved/restored so toolbar controls that steal focus (color picker, selects) still apply to the right range. A **live preview** panel renders exactly `safeHtml(currentHtml)`. Toggles: enable signature, include on replies/forwards, and placement (segmented control: below/above quoted text).

### HTML sanitization end-to-end (reusing existing `safeHtml`)
- **On edit/preview:** client sanitizes with `safeHtml` for the live preview.
- **On save:** client sanitizes the editor HTML, then `saveMailboxSettings` sanitizes again server-side before storing into `signatureHtml`, and derives the plain-text `signature` via new `signatureHtmlToText` (in the new shared plain module `lib/mail/signature.ts`).
- **On send:** `Composer` re-sanitizes `signatureHtml` a third time before building the outgoing HTML part (defense in depth).
`safeHtml` strips script/style/iframe/on*/unsafe schemes; note `data:` URIs are among the neutered schemes, so inline data-URI images are removed — the editor therefore offers image-by-URL (https) only, and the UI states this honestly.

### Section status (honest)
1. **Signature** — real, fully wired into sending.
2. **Identity** — real: display name, `organization`, validated `replyTo`, read-only sending address.
3. **Auto-reply** — **store-only** (kept the existing amber notice); added a validated date range (`autoReplyStart`/`autoReplyEnd`). `lib/mailcow.ts` exposes no vacation/auto-responder endpoint, so it honestly does not claim to send.
4. **Forwarding** — **store-only** with an honest amber notice. I deliberately did not fake a Mailcow mechanism: an alias whose address equals an existing mailbox is rejected by Mailcow, and driving SOGo sieve is out of API scope, so `saveForwarding` persists `forwardingAddress` + `forwardKeepCopy` and clearly says mail is not yet auto-forwarded.
5. **Storage** — real meter using live IMAP usage already computed by `getMailboxes()` (passed as props from `MailClient`), falling back to the DB `quotaMB` with a note when live usage is unavailable.
6. **Connection / Aliases / Password** — kept as-is with light polish (shared `Toggle` extraction, new nav icons). Aliases still use `mcListAliases`/`mcAddAlias`/`mcDeleteAlias`; password still uses the existing owner-checked reset (`mcSetMailboxPassword`).

### Signature into outgoing mail — `MailClient.tsx` + `Composer.tsx`
`MailClient` loads a per-mailbox `SigConfig` (`getMailboxSettings`) on mount and on mailbox switch. A `sigFields(isReply)` helper spreads `signature`/`signatureHtml`/`signaturePlacement` into the draft only when enabled (and for replies/forwards only when `signatureOnReply`). New messages no longer inline the signature into the editable text — `Composer` appends the sanitized signature HTML to the HTML part and the plain-text version to the text part. For replies/forwards, placement controls whether the signature sits above or below the quoted `<blockquote>`. If only the legacy plain `signature` exists (no HTML), Composer falls back to the old `-- ` plain-text block.

### Actions — `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts`
`MailboxSettings` grew to carry all new fields (dates serialized as `YYYY-MM-DD`). `saveMailboxSettings` now does presence-based partial updates (Identity and Signature sub-forms save independently without clobbering each other), sanitizes signature HTML + derives plain text. Added `saveForwarding`; extended `saveAutoReply` with the validated date window. All keep `resolveMailbox` ownership checks + the existing rate-limit `gate`. Shared consts/types live in the plain module `lib/mail/signature.ts` (not the `"use server"` file).

### Mailcow endpoints used
No new Mailcow calls were added. Existing ones remain: aliases (`/get/alias/all`, `/add/alias`, `/delete/alias`) and password reset (`/edit/mailbox`). Storage reads live usage via IMAP `getQuota` (already in `getMailboxes`), not Mailcow.

No migration/resize/terminal/cPanel files were touched.
